name: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
thesis: Invests in bold founders building software that transforms major industries. Strong focus on AI infrastructure, developer tools, and the future of work.
why_good_fit: a16z has a dedicated AI fund and actively backs AI-native GTM tools. Their portfolio includes companies reinventing sales and marketing workflows with AI.

name: Sequoia Capital
thesis: Partners with founders from idea through IPO. Thesis spans AI, enterprise software, consumer, and fintech. Known for long-term conviction bets.
why_good_fit: Sequoia's Arc program actively scouts early AI companies. They've backed multiple AI-powered outbound and sales intelligence platforms.

name: First Round Capital
thesis: Seed-stage specialist focused on software and internet companies. Deep operational support network and community for founders.
why_good_fit: First Round is the go-to seed fund for B2B SaaS and AI tooling. Their portfolio companies are heavy users of AI-driven sales automation.

name: General Catalyst
thesis: Backs founders building enduring, mission-driven companies. Deep focus on AI, enterprise, healthcare, and climate. Emphasizes 'responsible innovation'.
why_good_fit: GC is aggressively investing in AI-native workflow tools for sales and marketing teams. Their enterprise-friendly approach aligns well with B2B go-to-market.

name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
thesis: Global multistage firm investing across enterprise, consumer, fintech, and health. Strong AI thesis with dedicated AI fund.
why_good_fit: Lightspeed has backed numerous AI-first GTM and sales tools. Their enterprise SaaS network provides warm intro paths to pilot customers.

name: Accel
thesis: Early-stage focus on enterprise software, security, and consumer. Invests globally with offices in London and Bangalore. Strong track record in B2B SaaS.
why_good_fit: Accel has a long history of backing sales and marketing infrastructure companies. Their Eurozone network is a plus for international expansion.

name: Greylock Partners
thesis: Enterprise-first fund with deep roots in developer tools, AI, and networked products. Founders-first culture with extensive talent network.
why_good_fit: Greylock invested in LinkedIn and understands professional network data deeply — highly relevant to AI-driven outreach tools leveraging contact intelligence.

name: Bessemer Venture Partners
thesis: Cloud-first investor known for 'anti-portfolio' transparency. Deep expertise in vertical SaaS, security, and AI applications for the enterprise.
why_good_fit: BVP publishes detailed cloud benchmarks and is a trusted partner for B2B SaaS founders. Their roadmap actively includes AI-augmented sales and prospecting tools.

name: Emergence Capital
thesis: Exclusively focused on enterprise cloud and the future of work. Coined the term 'cloud computing' and backed Salesforce, Zoom, and Veeva.
why_good_fit: Emergence is the canonical enterprise SaaS fund. AI-powered sales tools sit squarely in their 'coaching networks' thesis for transforming how teams work.

name: Craft Ventures
thesis: Founded by David Sacks (ex-PayPal/Yammer/Zenefits). Focus on B2B SaaS, AI applications, and enterprise productivity. Operationally heavy value-add.
why_good_fit: David Sacks is one of the most vocal advocates for AI-native sales tools. Craft actively helps portfolio companies implement AI-driven GTM strategies.

name: Point Nine Capital
thesis: Seed specialist exclusively focused on SaaS and marketplaces. Deep domain expertise in sales tools, CRMs, and B2B workflows across Europe and the US.
why_good_fit: Point Nine backed Zendesk, Pipedrive, and Typeform early. They understand sales stack deeply and are bullish on AI-first replacements for legacy tools.

name: Redpoint Ventures
thesis: Focuses on enterprise and consumer internet. Strong track record backing developer tools and infrastructure. Running dedicated GTM AI thesis.
why_good_fit: Redpoint's 'GTM Genius' initiative tracks every AI tool in the sales and marketing stack — they're actively looking for the next breakout in AI-powered prospecting.

name: Khosla Ventures
thesis: High-conviction bets on AI, deep tech, and enterprise transformation. Vinod Khosla is an outspoken AI bull — believes AI will replace most knowledge work.
why_good_fit: KV is one of the most aggressive AI investors. They're specifically looking for companies that use AI to 10x productivity in white-collar workflows like sales.

name: Felicis Ventures
thesis: Invests in outlier founders redefining large markets. Known for early bets in Canva, Shopify, and Credit Karma. Increasingly AI-focused.
why_good_fit: Felicis has backed multiple AI workflow tools targeting SMBs. Their network of revenue-generating portfolio companies is valuable for early enterprise pilots.

name: Insight Partners
thesis: Growth-stage specialist in high-growth software and internet companies. ScaleUp program provides hands-on GTM support for portfolio companies.
why_good_fit: Insight's ScaleUp methodology is specifically built for B2B SaaS. They help portfolio companies build repeatable sales motions — a natural fit for an AI-powered outreach platform.

name: GV (Google Ventures)
thesis: Alphabet's venture arm. Access to Google's AI/ML resources, infrastructure credits, and distribution. Invests across all stages and sectors.
why_good_fit: GV portfolio companies get preferential access to Google Workspace integrations and Google Cloud AI APIs — valuable for an email-heavy outreach product.

name: Benchmark
thesis: Small equal-partnership model. Every partner is fully engaged with every investment. Backs category-defining companies from the earliest stages.
why_good_fit: Benchmark is legendary for early product-market fit conviction. They backed Twitter, Uber, and Snap when unproven — exactly the kind of early bet needed here.

name: Index Ventures
thesis: Global fund with dual US-Europe presence. Invests in enterprise, fintech, and consumer. Deep playbook for scaling B2B from early traction to global.
why_good_fit: Index has a dedicated team for AI-native software and recently published a thesis on AI agents replacing outbound SDR teams — directly aligned.

name: Founders Fund
thesis: Peter Thiel's fund. Makes contrarian bets on companies building technologies most investors overlook. Strong anti-consensus stance on AI.
why_good_fit: Founders Fund is drawn to AI companies replacing entire job categories. AI-powered outbound that replaces full SDR teams is exactly the type of monopoly-scale vision they back.

name: Battery Ventures
thesis: Multistage fund focused on enterprise software, cloud infrastructure, and AI. Known for deep technical diligence and long hold periods.
why_good_fit: Battery has a strong GTM playbook for B2B SaaS and an active thesis around AI tools for revenue teams. Their portfolio includes multiple sales engagement platforms.

name: NEA
location: Chevy Chase, MD / Menlo Park, CA
thesis: One of the largest and oldest VC firms. Backs enterprise software, healthcare, and consumer. AI is now the centerpiece of their investment thesis.
why_good_fit: NEA's enterprise software team has deep relationships in sales ops, RevOps, and CRO functions at F500 companies — perfect for validating and distributing an AI outreach tool.

name: Base10 Partners
thesis: Invests in automation of the 'real economy' — sectors like logistics, healthcare, finance, and education being transformed by AI. Diversity-forward LP base.
why_good_fit: Base10's automation thesis maps directly to AI replacing manual outbound processes. They're seeking founders automating high-value repetitive workflows in B2B.

name: SV Angel
thesis: High-volume seed fund co-investing alongside top-tier VCs. Ron Conway's network provides unmatched intro access across Silicon Valley.
why_good_fit: SV Angel is the best door-opener in early-stage. Getting them in the round signals quality to follow-on investors and unlocks intros to Sequoia, a16z, and others.

name: Initialized Capital
thesis: Co-founded by Garry Tan (now YC president). Seed-stage focus on founders with unique insight. Heavy bias toward AI-native software companies.
why_good_fit: Initialized has deep YC ties and actively co-invests with YC batches. Strong portfolio overlap with B2B AI tools making them a natural fit for an AI outreach platform.

name: Coatue Management
thesis: Technology-focused crossover fund (public + private). Data-driven investment approach using proprietary analytics. Aggressively deploying into AI.
why_good_fit: Coatue leads large rounds for AI companies with clear revenue traction. Once an AI outreach product hits $1M ARR, Coatue is well-positioned to lead the Series A at scale.
